DESIGNER — MANISH — MOKOBARA - 24K MOKOGRAM LINE - DIWALI VISUALS

Mokobara - 24K Mokogram Line

Two deliverables for Mokobara's design task: a Diwali campaign and a modular sale unit system.

ROLE
Junior Designer (applicant)
BRAND
Mokobara
TOOLS
Figma, Higgsfield, GPT image gen
PROCESS
A few decisions behind the work.
01

Light as a principle, not a prop

Diwali is "the festival of lights," but most festive creative treats that literally — diyas, string lights, gold confetti. I wanted light to do actual work instead of decorate: catching the weave of the mokogram pattern, pooling around the product instead of flooding the frame, implying warmth without naming it outright.

02

Restraint over maximalism

The brief specifically asked for something beyond gold-on-black. So colour stayed deliberate — most of each frame sits in shadow or neutral tone, and gold only shows up where it's earned: on the product, on a highlight, never as a blanket backdrop.

03

Recreating the mokogram, by hand

To keep the pattern consistent across product shapes and colourways — rather than relying on whatever an AI model guessed the weave should look like — I rebuilt the mokogram pattern myself in three colourways, so every generated shot had a correct monogram to reference.

The rebuilt mokogram weave — gold-on-burgundy, gold-on-black, gold-on-navy.
04

AI-assisted production

The imagery was created using Higgsfield AI and GPT image tools, with creative direction across composition, product positioning, camera angles, lighting, and overall mood. Multiple references were used to build each shot, while the recreated Mokogram pattern was fed in as a reference to keep the product texture accurate and consistent across the campaign.

DELIVERABLE 02

Each piece has a fixed place and hierarchy, so prices, discounts and badges can change without rebuilding the layout.

Same visual language, different values. The system stays consistent across products.
